title: Configuring Border Radius
ques: Demonstrate the range of Tailwind **border radius** utilities: `rounded-none`, `rounded-md`, `rounded-2xl`, and `rounded-full`.
explanation: `rounded-*` utilities control `border-radius`. `rounded-md` is standard for buttons and inputs, `rounded-2xl` is common for modern cards, and `rounded-full` creates pill buttons or circular avatars.

title: Styling Border Colors
ques: Demonstrate the pairing of **border colors** with state pseudo-classes (`border-gray-300`, `focus:border-indigo-500`) on a text input element.
explanation: Border colors inherit Tailwind's color palette and can transition smoothly on interactive states like hover, focus, and validation errors.

title: Applying Box Shadows for Elevation
ques: Explain the shadow elevation scale (`shadow-sm`, `shadow-md`, `shadow-xl`, `shadow-2xl`) and write an interactive card that elevates smoothly on hover.

title: Controlling Opacity
ques: Demonstrate element opacity (`opacity-50`, `opacity-100`) and disabled button styling using Tailwind's `disabled:opacity-50` modifier.

answer.content:
<button 
  disabled 
  class="px-5 py-2.5 bg-blue-600 text-white font-medium rounded-lg transition-opacity disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed"
>
  Processing Order...
</button>

explanation: `opacity-*` utilities set the CSS `opacity` property from 0 to 100. The `disabled:opacity-50` variant instantly conveys inactive or pending state to users.

title: Focus Rings and Offset Utilities
ques: Explain the advantage of **Ring utilities** (`ring`, `ring-offset-2`) over standard CSS outlines for accessible focus indicators.

answer.content:
<!-- Accessible button with an indigo focus ring and white offset spacer -->
<button class="px-4 py-2 bg-indigo-600 text-white rounded-md font-semibold focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-indigo-500 focus:ring-offset-2 focus:ring-offset-white">
  Save Changes
</button>

explanation: Tailwind rings use `box-shadow` instead of CSS outlines. They perfectly conform to border radiuses and support `ring-offset-*` to render a clean gap between the element and the ring.
